hints: For each single number, there are only two possibilities in a selection. How many selections does that give in total?
Recursion with an include/exclude choice per element (or backtracking). Keep a current list; at index i either skip items[i] or add it, recurse, then remove it.

1. Start with an empty cur list and an empty result list.
  2. Define go(i): if i == n, add a copy of cur to the result and return.
  3. Exclude: call go(i+1).
  4. Include: add items[i] to cur, call go(i+1), then remove it (undo).
  5. Call go(0) and return the result.

approaches.name: Bitmask enumeration
approaches.idea: Loop masks 0..2ⁿ−1 and build the selection from the set bits. Equally fast, less recursive insight.

approaches.name: Optimal: include/exclude recursion
approaches.idea: Each element branches into two, giving exactly 2ⁿ leaves.

explain: For [4,7,1] the recursion tree has 3 levels of yes/no choices and 8 leaves, one per selection: [], [1], [7], [7,1], [4], [4,1], [4,7], [4,7,1]. Copying cur at each leaf is essential because the same list object keeps changing. The undo step (remove last) restores cur for the sibling branch. Output size itself is n·2ⁿ, so no solution can be faster.
recognize: 'Return every possible selection / subset' → each element is in or out, so branch twice per element (2ⁿ results).
javascript: function subsets(items) { let res = [[]]; for (const x of items) res = res.concat(res.map(s => [...s, x])); return res; }
